📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • With World of Warcraft: Forever's first raids set to release in early December, developers of the game have spoken about endgame itemisation and their desire to disrupt the "best-in-slot" (BIS) mindset that's been at the core of WoW's progression for years.
  • This information stems from the latest episode of the official World of Warcraft: Forever podcast.
  • Recent findings suggest that "I essentially want to get rid of BIS," Moon stated.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With World of Warcraft: Forever's first raids set to release in early December, developers of the game have spoken about endgame itemisation and their desire to disrupt the "best-in-slot" (BIS) mindset that's been at the core of WoW's progression for years.

This information stems from the latest episode of the official World of Warcraft: Forever podcast. In it, senior game designer Aidan Moon revealed his philosophy around the game's itemisation, which he played - and plays - a major role in designing.

Recent findings suggest that "I essentially want to get rid of BIS," Moon stated. "I think BIS is not a good thing for a video game that's supposed to be about role-playing. That's why I've introduced the creature subtype system, where things are more effective against murlocs [for example]. We've introduced the biome system too, and in the raid it's different.".

He gave an example from upcoming raid Barrow Deeps, which will be split into different biomes that offer opportunities for such creature subtype gear to be put to use. "If you go to the left wing that's snowy; if you go to the right wing, that's haunted; if you go down below, that's cavernous. ... I think your BIS should be different for every single boss if you're making a theoretical BIS list.".

Industry observers note that moon acknowledged that the system is open for players to interact with to the extent they're comfortable with. Some players might bring optimised gear for certain bosses, while others might not, opting instead for generally good gear to perform well regardless of the fight.

In a recent development, it's an excitingly different approach that goes against the established norms of WoW's endgame raiding. In other versions in World of Warcraft, gear progression is more linear: people go into raids with an idea of what gear drops are best for their character, and intentionally hunt these pieces to replace the set they're wearing. It's a vertical sense of progression. Will theoretically having multiple sets of equipment, for multiple situations, change this?

Best-in-slot gear is an especially pertinent topic in WoW Forever at the moment, given the most dedicated players are reaching max level, or nearing it, and are hunting for items in preparation for the upcoming raid. I'm at the moment ticking off equipment from a best-in-slot list for a Balance Druid. Whether this player behavior will change when the changes are implemented remains to be seen. Perhaps the approach will expand, with players continuing to hunt down generally accepted 'good' items while also seeking side pieces that provide situational bonuses along the way.

It has been revealed that the Blizzard discussion on raid itemisation went beyond standard power items. Chase items, those with especially low drop rates, were also talked about by Moon, noting that Barrow Deeps continues several such items that he hopes will keep players returning to it for years to come.

The items Moon is likely referring to here probably relate to mounts, pets, situational gear, and perhaps campfire bonuses.

For example, I obtained an upgraded campfire earlier in the game that allows a greater campfire to be built that allows more buff items to be placed around it.This has essentially locked me in as a campfire slave for the upcoming raid tier, and valuable to a raid composition.

World of Warcraft: Forever has proven extremely popular since its early November release. The game broke franchise records for Blizzard on launch, and has more weekly players than WoW has seen in 15 years. Judging from early impressions of World of Warcraft: Forever, the game has real merit.

Breaking: Feature: Seven Improvements We'd Still Love To See In GTA 6

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1165 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Purexbox

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, there's no two ways about it: GTA VI is a blummin' brilliant game, well worthy of its universally acclaimed 99 Metacritic score.
  • Both Fraser and I have put many hours into this enormous RPG already, and have come away floored by its grandeur.
  • We've whipped up a few of our own suggestions and mixed in some from across the world wide webbies to bring you our top improvements we'd like to see in GTA VI.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, there's no two ways about it: GTA VI is a blummin' brilliant game, well worthy of its universally acclaimed 99 Metacritic score. But just because we gave it a 10/10 here at Pure Xbox doesn't mean there isn't still some wiggle room for improvement.

Both Fraser and I have put many hours into this enormous RPG already, and have come away floored by its grandeur. However, we've also noticed a few things we'd like to see fixed or added to GTA VI to make it even better. Think of this article like adding marshmallows to a hot chocolate: we're looking to take something great and make it even sweeter.

We've whipped up a few of our own suggestions and mixed in some from across the world wide webbies to bring you our top improvements we'd like to see in GTA VI. Let's get into it:.

You've all noticed the darkness that appears from time to time around the screen, right? That's a vignette and GTA VI is a significant fan of them. It's most noticeable when you're booking it down the North 97 highway or, in the worst-case scenario, flying over the Keys as shown in the above screenshot.

GTA VI uses vignettes to cleverly draw your focus to the most crucial parts of the screen. I honestly think it's a great technique for making things feel more cinematic. Although, it is quite pants that there's no option to reduce its intensity or turn it off altogether. If Rockstar could give us the ability to toggle the vignette on and off, that would be great, because it also seems to be one of the most requested changes amongst GTA VI players.

Recent findings suggest that something I've grown increasingly aware of is the inability to wait or sleep to pass time across Leonida. I was particularly irked after an 18-hole crazy golf competition against Jason saw the sun set on us, and I didn't fancy driving all the way back to my lodging in Vice City. I wanted to pass time in my car or a nearby eatery, but my only option appeared to be the 4-5 minute drive home - made worse knowing that once morning hit, I'd just want to do the drive back and play golf in the daylight.

Recent findings suggest that it's probably the fault of Red Dead Redemption 2 and its extremely handy wilderness camps. They were great in a pinch to let you pass time swiftly. What would be great is if GTA VI gave players the option to rough it in their car for the night or find a nearby hotel room or something.

I was on a mission to pick up some prescription drugs when my car was escorted slowly into an enemy compound and the camera suddenly switched from third-person to first-person. Seeing Lucia's impeccable nails gripped around the steering wheel made me realise there's no legitimate way to drive from a behind-the-wheel perspective.

Sure, there's that glitch that lets you play GTA VI in first-person, but it would be better if Rockstar implemented an additional first-person POV for driving.

It seems like a bit of a no-brainer, but we'd love to see AMD FSR 4.1 implementation on Xbox Series X. GTA VI is already up-and-running with FSR 4.1 on Xbox Series S which brings internal resolutions up from 720p to 1080p output. It's good going on XSS, but we'd like to see what it can do with XSX.

If a game rolls out with a good Photo Mode, then you may as well tack an extra 10 hours onto my playthrough. But GTA VI? Maybe add another 20-30 hours. It's gorgeous!

Industry observers note that the Photo Mode in this game is already solid. You can set up light sources, adjust focus and aperture, and as a graduate photographer, I think it's all rather intuitive. There's even a selfie mode where players can pose Jason and Lucia together, adjust their facial expressions and change their poses.

What I'd like to see is that same flexibility expand beyond selfie mode. I'd like to be able to adjust the lovers to better match the photos I'm trying to create. It was during a tense getaway, four-stars and neck-deep in trouble, that I thought I'd take an action shot, only to find Jason had blinked and Lucia looked bored as hell. It would be great to have the option to adjust expressions, head directions, poses and all that sort of stuff.

Please fix the sliders when handling amounts of money, Rockstar. Please. It's not the biggest fix, nor the most elaborate, so I'll keep it brief.

Whenever I open my phone to buck myself some cash, I often struggle to select the right amount quickly. It takes too long for the slider to speed up as I increase the amount, but then it very quickly gets out of control, and I end up overshooting my intended figure. Plus, the sound it makes is quite horrid.

What would help is having set increments to scroll through, say, $1, $10, $50, $100 and so on. It might just smooth out the experience a smidge.

Sources indicate that I'd like to wrap up with a quickfire segment of some of our own suggestions on how Rockstar could improve GTA VI, but also some of yours. So, let's get through it.

I'd love to be able to call NPC buddies like Cal for a round of crazy golf. At the moment, playing with a partner is limited to Jason and Lucia. I'm all for love, but sometimes you need some friendly bonding too.

In a recent development, another one I'd personally like to see is custom music stations on in-game radios. Now, I know this isn't something likely to happen, but it would be cool to link my Spotify and Rockstar accounts to play my own curated playlists.

Sources indicate that oh, and for the love of all things matrimony, please let me make a coffee for Jason/Lucia and actually give it to them. I've experienced Jason asking for a cuppa joe, so let me do the do, y'know?

Sources indicate that something Fraser mentioned he'd like to see is additional minigames like bowling or darts added to the game. The developers said they ran out of time for things like this, so maybe they could add them as a post-launch enhancement.

And to wrap up, I've spotted folks online requesting the ability to dial any phone number like you could in previous games, as well as blind firing around cover during firefights, buying housing property, and having save states pick up directly where you left off.

According to recent reports, so, there you have it. Some of our suggestions and some we've found out in the wild, but we'd love to hear your ideas on what might make GTA VI a better game. Be sure to chat with us in the comments!

#133021. Industry News: Six Things You Should Do Now to Optimize Your Setup for GTA 6

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1153 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Six Things You Should Do Now to Optimize Your Setup for GTA 6

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1153 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • You’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI.
  • Sources indicate that GTA 6 is absurdly large.
  • Recent findings suggest that alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

You’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI. You’ve preloaded the game on your console, you’ve taken the next month off work, and you’ve locked your phone in a Faraday cage and set it adrift at sea. You’re prepared to lock in, and you haven’t forgotten a thing…right? Well, just to make sure, here are the most key tips to optimize your setup before you fire up the most anticipated game of the decade.

Sources indicate that GTA 6 is absurdly large. According to Rockstar, you’ll need up to 212GB of storage space. For high-end consoles like the PS5 Pro, that’s more than 10% of the available storage space, and close to half the space on the more budget-conscious Xbox Series S. There’s a good chance you’ll have to delete something to make room.

Recent findings suggest that alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it). External SSDs are probably the cheapest route, though you’ll want to make sure to use a high-speed USB cable to connect it. It’s even worth shopping around for alternate models of SSD. For example, at the time of writing, the popular 2TB WD_BLACK external drive was close to $200, but the exact same drive in pink was $132.

You can also directly upgrade the storage of your console with expansion drives. The Xbox Series X|S supports proprietary expansion cards, while the PS5 and PS5 Pro can accept most M.2 internal SSDs. These will generally be faster, since they plug directly into the console via higher-speed connections than a drive hooked up via USB.

Industry observers note that let’s face it: Half the fun of any sandbox game is the weird, unique stuff that happens to only you. So you’re probably going to be hitting that “record recent gameplay” button more often than usual. While you’re cleaning up your storage space (or adding more), make sure to account for all the video clips you might want to save.

Industry observers note that file size of video clips depends on a lot of factors, but 4K recordings can generally take up to 0.5GB per minute of footage. You can cut that down by saving footage in 1080p instead, but either way you’ll want to leave a little extra space.

Game footage is also a pretty good place to look if you need to make room on your console and don’t want to delete any games. Be honest with yourself: You don’t need all those clips from Horizon Forbidden West you saved four years ago. Dive into the settings on your console and find the biggest media files you forgot you even had on there.

According to Rockstar, GTA 6 will be targeting 30fps across consoles at launch, which is pretty low as modern AAA games go. Part of the reason for that is all the processing power going to rendering a complex environment, but it also means you won’t need a fancy high frame rate TV or monitor any time soon to get the most out of it. Still, it couldn’t hurt to check a few settings on your display.

First, make sure you’re using a higher refresh rate than 30Hz. While the game is targeting 30fps, it is technically capable of more, so if your console can keep up, you don’t want to accidentally bottleneck your frames. This setting will vary by device, so check the manual that came with your screen.

Industry observers note that also, make sure you have HDR enabled on your hardware. There’s a good chance this is already turned on for your TV, but sometimes other devices can switch display modes if they only support SDR. The game will help you calibrate your HDR settings for GTA 6 specifically when you launch it, but only if it detects HDR compatibility in the first place.

Industry observers note that if you’re planning to buy a console specifically for GTA 6, this might be one of those rare instances where a PS5 Pro really is worth the upgrade. According to Rockstar, certain features like ray-traced shadows will only be available on the Pro version of Sony’s console.

Sources indicate that more importantly, the PS5 Pro version supports PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (or PSSR), which upscales lower-resolution images to get better detail and higher frame rates out of the same hardware. Given that GTA 6 is already starting at a meager target of 30fps on most consoles, anything that can give your frame rate a boost is probably going to feel like a welcome improvement over the baseline.

Sources indicate that I’ll tell you a secret as someone who’s spent a lot of time testing different game controllers: Most of the time, you really don’t need an expensive “elite” controller. Most of the time. I don’t buy into the idea that a taller control stick is going to make you an esports athlete. It can be nice to have, but it’s not a game changer. What does matter is customizing your controls, especially for long gaming sessions.

Recent findings suggest that the DualSense Edge wireless controller is a favorite of mine, mainly because of the rear paddles and adjustable triggers. The former lets you map any button to a rear lever that you can access with your fingers underneath the controller, which can often ease some of the wrist strain of awkward button combos. And the adjustable triggers let you activate the buttons with less motion, again reducing repetitive stress.

The Xbox Elite Series 2 controller has similar features for the Xbox, as well as custom caps for the D-pad. Both consoles’ versions of pro controllers are more expensive than the standard ones, but if you’re planning to game for many hours, it can be worth it to get a controller that’s more comfortable for you.

In a recent development, if you have an Xbox One, you don’t necessarily have to upgrade your console to play GTA 6, but you might want to take a look at your network. GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on day one, and you’ll be able to stream the game to an Xbox One console (as long as you purchase Cloud playtime as well or get some with your Game Pass subscription). This is the only way to play on a console older than the current generation, so if you don’t want to shell out for upcoming hardware, this might be your best bet.

It has been revealed that xbox recommends a minimum of a 20Mbps connection to run cloud gaming, but more is obviously better. If you can connect your console to a wired Ethernet connection, that would be better and provide more stability. If you can’t connect a cable, then at least make sure you’re well within range of your wifi router, and try to limit any other bandwidth-hogging applications on the network while you’re playing.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Even though Sony has paid god-only-knows how much money to market GTA 6 as a borderline PS5 exclusive, it turns out that Rockstar's magnum opus actually runs better on Xbox.
  • This is according to those tech wizards over at Digital Foundry, who have spent hours comparing the open world title across base PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X, and Xbox Series S.
  • Now, we already know that GTA 6 isn't perfect on the standard PS5.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Even though Sony has paid god-only-knows how much money to market GTA 6 as a borderline PS5 exclusive, it turns out that Rockstar's magnum opus actually runs better on Xbox.

This is according to those tech wizards over at Digital Foundry, who have spent hours comparing the open world title across base PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X, and Xbox Series S.

Now, we already know that GTA 6 isn't perfect on the standard PS5. It suffers from minor but sometimes prolonged frame rate drops during busy scenes — whether you're speeding through heavy traffic or fighting for your life in a particularly explosive combat encounter.

Recent findings suggest that but in a rather shocking twist, the Xbox Series X outdoes the PS5 in this department. While Digital Foundry's testing highlights that the frame rate dips are still present on the Series X, they're nowhere near as frequent.

They write: "PS5 suffers substantially more frequent frame rate drops than Series X, which is compounded by the fact that the Xbox machine also benefits from 120Hz VRR support to smooth out minor dips.".

The article continues: "Ultimately, Series X is meaningfully better off.".

This isn't what you'd expect, given that every PlayStation-related GTA 6 advertisement and trailer has boasted that the game 'Plays Best on PS5'.

Okay, so that slogan might technically be true if we're counting the PS5 Pro, where GTA 6 does perform best by some distance, thanks to a combination of the console's PSSR upscaler and increased GPU power.

But on base hardware, it's Microsoft that wins out.

"Overall, the PS5 Pro leads the rankings with its superior visual detail and rock-solid 30fps target, followed by the Xbox Series X — which edges out the standard PS5 through better performance stability," Digital Foundry concludes.

Are you surprised by these findings? Have you noticed any frequent frame rate drops in GTA 6 on PS5? Wonder if we'll ever see 60fps again in the comments section below.

Industry observers note that as countless people flock to Grand Theft Auto 6 following its launch earlier this week, a common highlight gamers have been highlighting are the many radio stations present in the game. While packed with songs, one artist has expressed her frustration with not being included among the list of featured artists.

Doja Cat, a rap-pop artist and avid gamer, took to Twitter to vent about the situation. In three back-to-back posts, her thoughts were made especially clear.

"I would’ve loved to have my music on gta6 i’m so f****n bitter," She wrote. "@RockstarGames eat my d**k all yall I love your stupid f****n b***h *** game." Her final on the matter reads: "@RockstarGames.

you broke my heart p***e c****o".

Doja Cat has long been public about her love for the medium. She often streams games live on Twitch, including Fortnite, and is among the most popular Final Fantasy 14 streamers. She's also mentioned games in her songs, including a reference to Grand Theft Auto 6 in her song 'All Mine'.

Recent findings suggest that personal desires aside, having your music featured in Grand Theft Auto 6 has proven to be a rich opportunity for musicians. Tom Petty's Love is a Long Road soared by around 36 percent immediately after the release of a Grand Theft Auto 6 trailer in which it was included. So, the game acts as a spotlight on artists and their works.

Still, there is hope for Doja Cat and other artists who want their music included in the game. Rockstar Games has a history of expanding the number of songs featured on in-game radio stations post-launch as seen in Grand Theft Auto 5, so fingers crossed for the future.

If you're looking for some help getting through Grand Theft Auto 6, we've got a Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough you can read, as well as a breakdown of all the Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

Industry News: Space station horror-FPS Derelikt is a lively retro throwback to Alien: Resurrection, though it's better at shooting than scaring

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (711 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that I'm a reasonable man.
  • Sources indicate that still, Derelikt is fortunate that it's a good shooter, as it often gets muddled on whether it wants to be a horror game as well.
  • Industry observers note that but nah, shotgun go boom boom.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that I'm a reasonable man. I don't expect every PS1-styled, cosmic horror, nakedly Alien: Resurrection-homaging retro FPS to suffocate me under a blanket of misery. Some of the lighter moments in Derelikt, which released last week, even land: I was grinning my cheeks off as I gorged on the Eldtrich knowledge sealed within an alien obelisk, while repeatedly hanging up on the aghast scientist who kept videocalling me to stop.

Sources indicate that still, Derelikt is fortunate that it's a good shooter, as it often gets muddled on whether it wants to be a horror game as well. It certainly threatens the spooks, trapping you in an oppressively dingy asteroid rig in the orbit of Saturn - the scariest of the ringed gas giants! - and warping most of the other staff into vaguely echinodemic monsterpeople. Also, opening the inventory reveals it to be made of rectangles, a classic symptom of a video game character about to get mangled in the nerves and face.

Industry observers note that but nah, shotgun go boom boom. It turns out Derelikt's derelict dwellers are both perfectly susceptible to mundane lead, and sparing people of ambush tactics at most; several even stand around with their backs turned, as if waiting for you to surprise them with a lethal pipe swing. And, even on Medium difficulty, the opening spell of fight-or-run scarcity quickly gives way to an abundance of ammo and health pickups that can easily fill the pocket grid to bursting. I don't claim to have been playing perfectly, but I'm about halfway through and the only way I see myself running low on bullets is if I start using them to punch the complete works of Thomas Campion into a wall.

It's indecisive tonally, as well. The dialogue, and there are a fair few survivors to chat with, seems interested in emulating the gravitas-starved, "Woah man" style of Upcoming Millennium action game scripts. Which I can sort of see the logic behind, given the visuals and sound design also, and arguably much more painstakingly, mimic that era. But the downside remains that it ends up with a gravitas-starved, "Woah man" style, just with an extra dash of sideways-winking awareness. Again, it only sometimes works, and it's never scary or eerie. But then there are also more earnest attempts to spin uneasiness, with pages of deranged scribbles left behind by the dwindling crew, and at least a couple of genre-classic wall daubings, which tend to leave me wishing developers Visuwyg had just picked a lane.

It has been revealed that again, though, underneath all the smartarsing is a quality little shooter. The retro presentation does little to soften the heavy, industrial kick of its gunfire, and although many of the meatier freaks are more absorbent than they look, their pained thrashing really helps sell the impact of every individual shot. I also don't really mind the lack of Dead Spacey surprise attacks, as the station's narrow confines tend to force you into tenser, close-range encounters in an organic way anyhow.

In a recent development, more impressive still is how Derelikt manages to fabricate a cold, apprehensive atmosphere befitting its fallen space base, in direct defiance of its own quasi-comedic script. This is mainly thanks to the clanging, low-lit station itself, which teases you with just enough flashes of comfort – a stretch of marble floor here, a messy rec room there – to make your quick return to its steel guts feel all the more unpleasant. Some credit must also go to the puzzling, the cardkey hunts and code searches of which initially had me fearful of the more obstinate, opaque, classic horror style preferred by fellow backwards-looker Silver Pines. Instead, it's more like a compacted Deus Ex, hinting at the need to peek at people's computers and scour the environments for the needed codes. Which makes for generally smoother progress, yes, but also gets you more involved and present inside Derelikt's infested walls.

Midway-through impressions, then: it's a little silly, and perhaps a little confused, but Derelikt finds its focus whenever something needs making dead. I shall continue blasting xenos and burning my eyes out with magic rocks until – no, madam, please hold – further notice.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Gravity Well, an "anti-crunch" studio founded in 2020 by former Apex Legends executive producer Drew McCoy and lead software engineer Jon Shiring, is entering "hibernation" after losing funding for its game.

In a recent development, gravity Well's launch in 2020 came with high hopes. Founded by veterans of Call of Duty, Titanfall, and Apex Legends, it made the health of the team "an absolute top priority," McCoy mentioned at the time.

It has been revealed that "That means we are anti-crunch. That means good compensation. That means everyone at Gravity Well has creative freedom, because when someone else makes all of the decisions, work isn't fun and the end product isn't as good.".

But like so many other ambitious fresh studios debuted around that time, it fell victim to the post-pandemic retrenchment and has effectively shuttered without releasing a game. The shutdown comes just a month after the studio laid off more than 40 people in what it remarked was a "fight for survival" caused by the loss of funding. It also warned that "given the current state of the industry our future is uncertain.".

A message now posted on the Gravity Well website (via RPS) notes the funding situation hasn't changed, and "sadly the time has come for Gravity Well to go into hibernation.".

"We don’t exactly know what is next for us or Gravity Well, but we do know we still believe in the IP and game we were building," the message states. "Even moreso, the team we managed to cultivate was truly world class and we're going to miss getting to work with them every day. If you're a hiring manager or recruiter and a Gravity Well resume hits your desk they come with our highest recommendation.".

The announcement concludes with an invitation to publishers and investors to reach out if they're interested in supporting the project.

Grand Theft Auto 6 is estimated to have sold nearly 25 million copies in one day, generating approximately $2.5bn in sales revenue - a staggering result that's beyond even what even observers were predicting.

The estimates come from data-tracking company Sensor Tower (spotted by VGC), which has been watching GTA 6 pre-orders closely for weeks, updating estimates daily based on (unspecified) data that it collects.

According to recent reports, should the results be accurate, it'll dramatically eclipse GTA 6's $1bn in three days result. It'll also put GTA 6 on track to reach the eye-watering $3.25bn to $5.2bn week-one sales estimates for GTA 6.

So far, Rockstar has noted nothing in relation to GTA 6's sales since the game was released around the world yesterday. Parent organization Take-Two has said the game's pre-orders were tracking "well above expectations, and GTA 6 broke pre-order records on both the PlayStation Store and the Xbox Store, though, so all signs point to a record-breaking release. The question is "by how much?".

Reaction to GTA 6 has been glittering. Chris awarded GTA 6 five golden stars in Eurogamer's review, calling it "a game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale". "Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that.".

Black Friday is usually a great time to grab a upcoming e-reader, but the ongoing RAM crisis has made that a question mark this year: Amazon recently raised the prices of all its Kindles by around $50 and refreshed the entire lineup, which means your odds of grabbing one at a substantial discount are low. But you aren't totally out of luck: If you haven't noticed, micro-e-readers—I'm talking credit card-sized, with screens that measure around four inches—are all the rage in 2026, and right now, you can pick up one of them for around $55.

If you too can see the appeal of carrying all of your books with you on a device so small you'll forget it's even in your pocket, it's a great time to jump in: The recently released Xteink X4 Classic is currently 38% off for Black Friday, bringing it down to $54.87, a record-low price. Meanwhile, the smaller X3 is $55.72, or 19% off. Both are available in either "mist grey" or "space black." The discounts should last through the end of Cyber Monday on Nov. 30.

Xteink is a Chinese startup that shook up the e-reading world last year with the launch of the X4, a super bare-bones device that made up for its lack of features and usability with a cheap sub-$70 price point. Since then, a huge online community of fans has formed, sharing tips on Reddit and even coming together to crowdsource an alternate operating system that fixed a lot of early problems. Xteink swiftly followed up the X4 with a slate of other devices, including the 3.7-inch X3 and the X4 Pro, which adds a front light and touchscreen (at the cost of screen clarity and two physical buttons).

The X4 Classic and the X3 improve on the original X4 with quality-of-life upgrades like a larger battery, relocated page-turn buttons, a real-time clock, and a tilt-to-turn-page feature. They're also lighter and thinner than the X4, though there is a trade-off involved: They drop the USB-C charging port in favor of magnetic pogo pins that require a separate adapter (included).

These upgrades also increased the cost: The X4 Classic typically retails for $89, $20 more than the discontinued X4 and only $10 less than the X4 Pro, while the X3 debuted at $79. But right now, the X4 Classic is just under $55, or around 38% off, and the X3 is about a dollar more. Either is a great option for those who prioritize crisp, readable text above the conveniences of a built-in light or touchscreen, as those add extra layers between the inner screen and outer glass. It's also important to understand what you're getting into: These devices support only e-books without Digital Rights Management (DRM), which means you can't use it to read your existing library of Kindle books. On the plus side, there's no longer a need to worry about flashing new firmware if you don't want to, as the native version has been totally overhauled and is now one of your best options (though the new firmware, called "Licorice," isn't available on the X3 quite yet).

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Industry observers note that follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. For the majority of products, the deal from Black Friday will be the same one on Cyber Monday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Valve giveth, and Valve taketh away in their latest Steam Machine availability update. The dinky SteamOS PC continues to have a terrible time with AI industry-inflicted hardware parts shortages, which at least for its flagship 2TB model, have become such a problem that Valve are suspending new orders until further notice. While Valve's post indicates that they "have wrapped up sending purchase invites out to all remaining 2TB reservation holders" – meaning if you'd previously reserved one, you'll still get your chance to buy – "supply restraints" have put the kibosh on any new orders for now.

It's not all bad news, though. The cheaper 512GB Steam Machine has achieved "add-to-cart status", which is Valve's slightly odd way of saying you can snap one up without having to join a reservation waitlist. Just like in the Before Times! The post does add that 512GB stock is still limited, so that might sell out too if they can't source enough parts to build new ones, though this is still the first time that the refreshed Steam Machine has been waitlist-free since launching in June.

One could, with the aid of a Torx screwdriver and a conveniently illustrated guide, work around the 2TB model's lack of existence by nabbing a readily available 512GB Machine and replacing its stock SSD with a chunkier aftermarket drive. A not-terrible, budget two-gigster can be had from £240, which when added to the 512GB Machine's £879 outlay, actually works out a little less than buying a 2TB Machine as is. SteamOS is free to download and install, and swapping out the Steam Machine's SSD is considerably easier than the plasticky brain surgery of Steam Deck drive replacement.

According to recent reports, of course, ideally none of that would be necessary, and we could all fill our living rooms with sub-£700 Steam Machines that had never been choked by the greedy hands of industrial-scale RAM hoarders. But that's not the world we live in. Indeed, Valve end the post by rather chillingly suggesting that their hardware prices may rise yet again.

"We are continuing to build more Steam Machine units," they say, "but memory and storage costs continue to increase at unprecedented levels; as a result we don't yet know the number we are able to make, and at what price we'll be able to offer them. The 2TB model in particular will be especially constrained.".

"We anticipate having more information to share come January.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that there is perhaps nothing so brutal in a Total War game than getting an army full of elite units wiped out, and it appears that pain remains a factor in the upcoming Total War conversion of : Warhammer 40,000. Creative Assembly also has some nifty ideas around breaking the game into mini-campaigns for each star system you visit.

Industry observers note that in an hour-long deep-dive livestream of Total War: Warhammer 40,000, developer Creative Assembly demonstrated the game in action, focusing initially on how armies navigate from planet to planet. Each star system apparently acts as a "contained campaign" you can hop between in the game.

Recent findings suggest that the star system the stream focused on is Praevoss, a mid-sized collection of planets: three of which you can land on and fight on, while the others are smaller and unable to support your tactical warfare shenanigans. Once you're finished with a star system, you move on, carrying over units and unlocked skills.

"First and foremost, we want to represent the scale of the whole galaxy, which is just not possible on a single Total War map," Creative Assembly explained on the livestream. "You'd never be able to engage with it. Part of the point is to break this up a bit and allow us to have some more interesting and more bespoke narratives going on. So each of these star systems has a premise, has a narrative, has a specific setup, a specific start, [and] specific victory objectives that you've got to go and do.".

One of the objectives highlighted in the livestream was an Ork Scourge, which required the player - controlling Space Marines - to hold the planet while eradicating the Ork presence.

Recent findings suggest that as you can imagine, much of the stream was dedicated to the fleet of spaceships at your disposal - fleet movement and management, and the abilities they provide to your armies such as orbital bombardments. There was also detail on how ships transport troops, as well as the upgrades you can build to further enhance their power.

On the topic of transporting troops, the developers focused on the small number of expensive but powerful Space Marines they controlled. These Space Marine armies come with a potentially "devastating" cost if you mess up and lose your armies during one of the star system campaigns.

"Losing a whole army of Space Marines is pretty devastating," the developers explained. "That's intentional, as that's a whole Space Marine chapter. Like, losing an army of Space Marines, that's a massive deal for them. It would take them decades to recover from that.".

In a recent development, total War: Warhammer 40,000 is set to release some time in 2027, though no specific date has been established as of writing. Much has been seen at this point on its gameplay, galactic or otherwise. As we near the end of the year, fans are clamouring for official word on when they can take to the stars.

It has been revealed that robert Pattinson was just revealed as the next James Bond, and the internet has spent the days since joking that no Hollywood role is safe from him. I thought those jokes had about run their course until Ralph Fiennes weighed in. The actor who terrified an entire generation of Harry Potter fans as Lord Voldemort was asked who should take over the role in HBO's upcoming television series, and his answer was so dry that I almost missed how funny it was.

Pattinson played Cedric Diggory in 2005's Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire, the same film that introduced Fiennes as the fully resurrected Voldemort. Cedric made it through the Triwizard Tournament only to be murdered by Peter Pettigrew on Voldemort's orders. It's a miserable ending for one of the story's most likable characters.

In a recent development, so imagine the actor who played Cedric now taking over as the man who ordered his death. I'd almost pay to see Pattinson in the makeup just for that bit of full-circle casting, although I'm pretty sure Fiennes was having a laugh rather than making a serious recommendation.

The two actors also have a second franchise connection thanks to Bond. Fiennes played M opposite Daniel Craig in Skyfall, Spectre and No Time to Die, so he's watched a different actor occupy the 007 role that Pattinson is now inheriting. The Tenet actor has already spent plenty of time bouncing between massive franchises, from Twilight to The Batman. It's getting hard to name an iconic fictional universe he hasn't visited.

Recent findings suggest that the actual casting of Voldemort remains a mystery. Fiennes previously mentioned he was all for Cillian Murphy playing the Dark Lord, and there's been no shortage of rumors about who might portray the villain. He's also offered the eventual actor some practical advice on navigating Voldemort's robes. Whoever gets the job has quite a performance to follow.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

I'm excited to see who HBO chooses, but Fiennes has made me realize there's one more possibility I hadn't considered. If Pattinson somehow lands the role, he'll have played Cedric Diggory and the wizard who had him killed. At this rate, I'd hesitate to rule out anything.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that paying for access to online multiplayer has been the norm on Xbox consoles for decades now.
  • In a recent development, eight years ago, I bought a gaming laptop to play Battlefield V on the go, and ever since paying for access to online multiplayer hasn't made much sense to me.
  • In a recent development, xbox Play Anywhere is probably where console paywalls really start to look silly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that paying for access to online multiplayer has been the norm on Xbox consoles for decades now. It's something we've come to expect as part of playing online with friends and other folk around the world. The general understanding is, if you don't have Xbox Live, you're not playing online.

In a recent development, eight years ago, I bought a gaming laptop to play Battlefield V on the go, and ever since paying for access to online multiplayer hasn't made much sense to me. It's just not something you do on PC. Sure, games like World of Warcraft and Final Fantasy XIV require additional subscriptions in order to play, but the majority of online games, like BFV, only require you to upfront the retail cost and crack on.

In a recent development, xbox Play Anywhere is probably where console paywalls really start to look silly. Just a few months ago, I bought Subnautica 2 to play with a friend through the Xbox PC app. I could've opted for Steam, but I wanted to work towards those Xbox cheevos (when they eventually arrive). For a couple of weeks, I'd hop on the PC and dive into alien waters with my mate.

In a recent development, one day, I fancied playing on the significant screen in my living room, so I installed Subnautica 2 on my Xbox Series X, booted it up and was prompted to buy a Game Pass subscription just to play the same save file I'd been enjoying for weeks through the Xbox PC app. Like I said, a bit silly.

Time went on, and I'd more or less let this go from my head until I read a report from Windows Central a couple days ago, claiming that Microsoft's upcoming Xbox Helix next-gen console could have intends to kill paywalls for paid multiplayer.

"Sources close to Microsoft's prepares tell me Xbox Helix was originally conceived as a true console-PC hybrid with access to Windows PC games and stores such as Steam, alongside another major change: no paywall for online multiplayer.".

According to Jez Corden, the original blueprint for Xbox Helix was to create a console-PC hybrid with access to Steam, potentially spelling the end of Xbox's staple multiplayer charges. It kind of makes sense when you think about it. If you can play your Xbox games across both console and PC, whether through disc-to-digital or Xbox Play Anywhere, it seems like pointless friction to lock multiplayer behind a paywall depending on which device you're playing on.

Back in 2021, changes to Xbox's paid multiplayer requirements allowed players without an active Xbox Live Gold subscription to access multiplayer free-to-play titles such as Fortnite, Call of Duty: Warzone and Apex Legends. And today, Xbox Live Gold isn't even a thing, as it's been absorbed into Xbox Game Pass.

So, even if Xbox Helix's original vision has changed somewhat from what Corden initially reported, it's still not out of the question to suggest that paid multiplayer could eventually become redundant.

Pure Xbox, we'd love to hear what you think about this. Make sure to vote in the poll below and tell us more in the comments section.

In a recent development, grand Theft Auto 6's seismic launch has registered on a governmental level. A spokesperson for UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has hailed the game as a "British success story", but confirmed Burnham himself won't be playing it. His diary is apparently "very full".

According to recent reports, "Rockstar Games is a British success story made in Edinburgh," a Downing Street spokesperson told The Independent - referencing the series' Scottish origins and ongoing development at Rockstar North - "and many fans are already saying GTA has been worth the wait." When asked if Burnham will be making time for GTA 6, the spokesperson responded: "His diary is very full. He won't be playing it.".

Downing Street went on to address the problem of teenagers potentially skipping school to play the game, emphasising that children "should be in classrooms" this week because "every day in school matters".

It has been revealed that the leader of Labour's opposition, the Conservative party's Kemi Badendoch, recently expressed similar concerns. "I know people are worried about the game content," she wrote. "At the same time, I'd be more worried about a kid who played it all day, who was in their bedroom all day, than one who spends half-an-hour on it and then went out and did something else.".

GTA 6's culture-shaking success was unlikely to pass without reference by the government, but the celebratory tone is a marked departure from Burnham's predecessor Kier Starmer calling Rockstar's firing of 34 staff last year "deeply concerning". We are awaiting a verdict in the resulting employment tribunal related to it.

Recent findings suggest that this state recognition of GTA 6 is not without precedent. It wasn't long ago that French President Emmanuel Macron congratulated Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 on its award-winning and heart-winning success. That game sold 8 million copies in one year; GTA 6 is estimated to have sold 25 million copies in one day.

GTA 6 has been hailed as a generational release - an exorbitantly luxurious game that "pushes back the horizon of video games", Chris Tapsell wrote in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft have revealed their Motherbrain. It's far less cool than it sounds. Rather than being a giant floating slab of thinky meat that can do telepathy, Motherbrain is a studio dedicated to doing development stuff with generative AI. As you might expect, it consists of the folks who worked on Ubisoft's "first playable generative AI experience".

In a recent development, motherbrain's reveal as "a dedicated subsidiary focused on AI for gameplay innovation" came via Ubisoft's latest earnings report, where the firm trumpeted that their "upcoming operating model" is "now fully in place". The model is the reorganising into creative houses responsible for different game series that Ubisoft unveiled at the start of this year, with leaders for all of the houses now arranged.

"We have also established Motherbrain, the team behind our first playable generative AI experience Teammates, as a dedicated subsidiary developing proprietary technologies for gameplay to empower creators and open up new possibilities for richer, more immersive and engaging player experiences," CEO Yves Guillemot noted.

You'll never guess what his next few lines were. "We remain on track with our cost reduction program, reflecting our commitment to a focused and disciplined organization as we are preparing for a significantly stronger content cycle," the exec said. "In parallel, we have made progress on our refinancing plan with the objective of securing competitive terms and putting in place an efficient medium-term plan over the coming months.".

Recent findings suggest that that'd be the wave of layoffs and closures Ubisoft have been rolling out all through this year, most recently getting rid of 166 staff at Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec, both of which worked on Assassin's Creed Shadows. Ubisoft Singapore and Trials developers Redlynx, Ubisoft Winnipeg, Belgrade, and Barcelona, long-time Tom Clancy studio Red Storm, Ubisoft's Paris HQ and three German studios including Anno devs Ubisoft Mainz are all on the list of bits of the company affected in some way by the cuts.

Changes to remote working policies have also contributed to strikes at Ubisoft studios in France and Italy.

Ah well, at least there's seemingly money there to support the developing of those proprietary technologies infused with genAI brainiacery.

The combination of his unexpected swagger and ridiculous high-pitched Huttese monologues - performed irresistibly by actor Richard Summers-Calvert - have made him a fan favourite, especially his catchphrase "scrib doon" (which means "write it down").

It has been revealed that "Here's a name for you, amateur!" Blas tells the player upon meeting them, albeit in Huttese. "Biddy Blas. Write it down. Tattoo it on your arm, and someday your arm will be worth millions!".

"He was an incredibly enjoyable character to build, from our early ideation of a small, angry non-human character (who we lovingly referred to as our cast's 'chaos goblin') to recording his sometimes-absurdist dialogue with Blas' voice actor, who took the crocin to a whole fresh level.

"It's been great watching Biddy Blas emerge into his assured self, as well as seeing the community embrace him for it. He's always known exactly who he is, and he wears it proudly.".

According to recent reports, blas' breakout success was praised by Lucasfilm producer Craig Derrick, who said his social feeds were filled with posts about Galactic Racer, though mostly about Biddy Blas. And the enthusiasm actor Richard Summers-Calvert was greeted with during October's MCM Comic-Con in London, which I attended, was palpable. There's a nice video of him doing Blas' voice on Instagram.

According to recent reports, star Wars: Galactic Racer was awarded a full five stars in Eurogamer's review. "Both a surprisingly fun Roguelite campaign and a racing treat for Criterion fans, this is just wonderful stuff," wrote Christian Donlan.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Kurabayashi initially worked as a programmer on smaller titles at Taito, including early 2.5D fighting game Fighters' Impact (later localised as VS.
  • Recent findings suggest that fighting EX Layer started out as an April Fools' joke back in 2017, but the reaction to the trailer from fans who missed the SFEX series convinced Arika to bring the series back, even without the Capcom IP.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As declared in a statement by Arika president Akira Nishitani (and translated by Time Extension, thank you), Akira Kurabayashi, a director at the combined dev/publishing studio and a creator whose work spans three decades and several genres, sadly passed away as a result of heart failure late last week.

Kurabayashi initially worked as a programmer on smaller titles at Taito, including early 2.5D fighting game Fighters' Impact (later localised as VS. in America). He then moved to Arika in 1996 and continued his work in 2.5D fighters with the Street Fighter EX series, a subseries which took the originator of the fighting game genre into the third dimension for the first time. While that subseries didn't last long, its spiritual successor Fighting EX Layer made waves in 2018, bringing back original characters from SFEX and even including Fatal Fury's Terry Bogard.

Recent findings suggest that fighting EX Layer started out as an April Fools' joke back in 2017, but the reaction to the trailer from fans who missed the SFEX series convinced Arika to bring the series back, even without the Capcom IP. The final result is an interesting 2.5D fighter that combines conventional mechanics, such as magic series combos and supers, with the unique (for better and worse) Gougi system, where of in-match perks are chosen from a deck of cards at roundstart. I had a good time playing it for its systems (and Terry is very fun in it), but the Gougi system brought to mind Street Fighter x Tekken's infamous paid Gem debacle, which no one should be reminded of. Anyway. In addition to 2.5D fighters, Kurabayashi also contributed to Tetris: The Grandmaster, Tetris 99, PAC-MAN 99, and ARIKA's collaboration with SNK in the form of their 'SNK Revamp Project'.

Nishitani gave a few personal words towards Kurabayashi in the statement:.

In a recent development, "We are deeply saddened to have lost a dear colleague who has created numerous works with us and supported Arika for many years. We express our heartfelt respect and gratitude for his immense achievements to date, and we will cherish and carry on the skills, experience, and attitude toward game development that he left behind. I would like to express my deepest gratitude for the kindness you revealed us during their lifetime, and I respectfully pray for the repose of their soul.".

Condolences to Kurabayashi's family.

Industry observers note that that's where the iPad A16 comes in. This is Apple's least expensive tablet, with an MSRP of $449. But despite being Apple's "budget" option, the iPad A16 shouldn't be ignored by customers looking for the best all-around device. In fact, it's really the best iPad for most people, which is why I named it the best tablet gift of 2026. What's more, retailers are giving the iPad A16 a $50 discount ahead of Black Friday, bringing the entry-level price down to $399.

The iPad A16 isn't Apple's best iPad (that would be the iPad Pro). It doesn't have the best display, the best camera, or the best processor. But it doesn't need those things: This iPad has a display, camera, and processor that are good enough for most use cases, without unnecessarily driving up the price. Simply put, it's one of the best tablets you can buy right now.

It has been revealed that the iPad A16 has a large, 11-inch (technically 10.86 inches, according to Apple's fine print) IPS display with a brightness of 500 nits. As the name implies, it has Apple's A16 chip, the same processor as the iPhone 14 Pro and iPhone 15. That chip is about four years old at this point, and while that means it won't be as fast as Apple's newer SoCs, it still holds its own with iOS 27. It comes with two cameras: One 12MP wide camera on the back, with support for 4K video recording, and a 12MP Center Stage camera on the front.

According to recent reports, apple claims this iPad can run for 10 hours while browsing the internet on wifi or watching video. You charge the tablet with USB-C, which supports data transfer up to USB 2.0 (which nets you 480Mb/s transfer speeds). It also comes with other perks you might expect from Apple's more "pro" tablets. You can connect the iPad to an external display, up to 4K resolution at 60Hz. It also supports two Apple Pencil models: The USB-C Apple Pencil and the first-gen Apple Pencil.

The only real consideration here is storage: This model comes with 128GB of storage, which can run out fast. It's particularly usable for people who rely on cloud storage or mostly stream their entertainment. But if your giftee looks to store photos, videos, or music on their iPad, it's worth considering upgrading. The $50 discount applies to most storage models, as well as the cellular iPad options, except for the 512GB models: The wifi-only model has a smaller discount, while the cellular option has a $100 discount.

Recent findings suggest that sure, the iPad A16 doesn't have the fastest processor, an OLED display, support for newer accessories, or Apple's sharpest cameras. But all of the specs it does have are enough to run the things you need on iPadOS. If someone on your list is looking for an iPad for web browsing, streaming, messaging, and light gaming—and they don't need something for professional work—this device is likely more than enough iPad for them.

One of the cars Randy wants in GTA 6 is the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular—and don't let the name fool you, its a slick and speedy ride that'll you'll be tempted to keep for yourself.

Industry observers note that but Randy doesn't know the locations of many of the cars on his wishlist, and can't point you to the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular: you just need to keep an eye out for it. Luckily, we spotted it ourselves, so just follow the simple steps below to find it.

Head to Belville: It's a town in Leonard County, in the central eastern part of the map, a bit south of Lake Leonida and north of La Perle.

Industry observers note that in the northern edge of Belville there's a little cluster of four homes laid out almost in an X pattern. The southernmost home of that cluster has a garage you can break into. Once you open the garage door, you'll see the white Ocelot Bloodless Jugular.

You'll need the key cloner to get in, which I assume you already have since you're doing jobs for Randy. No need to worry about the tracker, it's a standard one so it won't transmit your location to the cops. You still don't want to dawdle, because the owner of the car has a gun and he's not afraid to use it. He'll start shooting if he sees you boost the car.

Recent findings suggest that randy will pay you $10,615 for the Ocelot Bloodless Jugular. He'll pay an extra $5,000 if you bring it to him in pristine condition.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shortly it debuted back in 2009, Ryan Murphy's campy musical comedy Glee became a sensation. The series (which is streaming with a Hulu subscription) broke barriers in regards to LGBTQ+ representation, and also featured plenty of memorable musical numbers. The show has also been associated with a number of tragedies, with three main cast members having died, starting with Cory Monteith's death back in 2013. There's been chatter online about the "Glee curse" and now Tina actress Jenna Ushkowitz has issued a heartfelt response about that discourse.

According to recent reports, monteith's death broke the heart of fans and his coworkers alike, with the cast quickly putting together a tribute episode in the midst of their grief. Since then there's been more tragedies with this talented ensemble, such as Naya Rivera's death in 2020. While appearing on the podcast We Need To Talk with Paul C. Brunson, Ushkowitz shared her emotional reaction to folks insensitively talking about the Glee curse.

My response to the Glee curse, as it’s always been, is we are human. And to hear that people see this as a collective curse that’s like, ‘Who’s next?’ is so unkind. And it indicates the way in which we are able to just sit behind our computers and type off whatever we think we’re feeling in that moment without really connecting to what’s behind it and who’s on the other side.

Talk about honesty. While folks online might be talking about the show's curse with levity, the experience of those who actually worked on Glee is another one entirely. Real people died, not characters, which has been a source for quite a bit of pain by the rest of the cast. Those feelings remain to this day, case in point being Harry Shum Jr. honoring Naya Rivera this season on Dancing with the Stars.

In a recent development, in addition to the death of Rivera and Monteith, Puck actor Mark Salling committed suicide back in 2018 before going to prison for possession of child sexual abuse imagery. What's more, an entire docuseries called The Price of Glee was released in 2023 examining the "curse." In the same podcast, Jenna Ushkowitz spoke more about the pain and grief that the cast has dealt with, offering:.

We lost friends. People grieve those people. This is not something that’s, like, ‘Who’s next? This is a game.’ It’s not.

In a recent development, the internet can be a cruel place, and the discourse about the Glee curse has clearly been painful for the cast. The tragic loss of their coworkers is hard enough, but the light-hearted chatter about these deaths has clearly created more pain for the members of the William McKinley High School Glee Club. Hopefully Ushkowitz's comments will circulate online, and help to quiet that type of talk.

Industry observers note that glee is streaming in its entirety over on Hulu, while fans patiently wait for news about Ryan Murphy's potential reboot. Our thoughts continue to be with the cast as they process their grief.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

One of the best things to emerge from Grand Theft Auto over the years has been the community's truly spectacular stunts: players soaring under bridges, leaping across buildings, and more. And with GTA 6's release this week, we've seen the first signs of the trend continuing in a brand-new world.

This TikTok video by user Gstitz from early in GTA 6, for instance, claims to be the "world's first" demonstration of a Mallard flying sideways between a narrow gap in a large building. It takes several attempts, but they eventually pull off the stunt without crashing or broken parts.

Another video from Hazardous is a more grounded (literally) look at Grand Theft Auto 6, and shows the YouTuber flinging motorbikes and cars around the map as they explore promising high-risk jumps. Some of these locations are tied to in-game challenges, so there are certainly breadcrumbs placed by Rockstar to encourage such ventures.

It has been revealed that granted, these are far from the truly absurd stunts we've seen in prior Grand Theft Auto games. But as a firing gun for the wider community, it's a great start. They're also among the most impressive things we've seen in GTA 6's opening week.

Sources indicate that it's doubtless been an eventful few days though. Players have been entranced by the slapstick violence and in-game social media. Even UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham has praised the game, despite not having time to actually play it. Eurogamer editor-in-chief Chris Tapsell also came away impressed, lauding it in his five star GTA 6 review.

If you're playing the game and need some help, you can read Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough, and our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheat list.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For the past six years, the team at RPS have got together to pick what we consider to be the best 100 games you can play on PC. There's very little science involved, and we try not to get too hung up on what games should make the cut. From year to year, our rankings and choices vary wildly as the formation and tastes of the team changes.

According to recent reports, however, our definitive list isn't always met with a chorus of approval and cheers of 'Hear, hear!', "'Well done!', and 'Couldn't have remarked it better myself!', so we also have the RPS 100: Reader Edition. This is your chance to submit your ten favourite PC games of all time. Your votes will be tallied up with all the other submissions from our other readers and we will produce a list of the community's top 100.

We've just finished revealing what we currently consider to be the Best PC games of all time and now it's your turn.

Using this very Google Form you can submit up to ten votes for your favourite PC games of all time. I will then tally them up with all the other votes from RPS's readers and produce a list of the community's top 100.

Now, a note on scoring. The game you put in 10th place will be awarded one point, 9th place will be worth two, 8th place will be worth three, and so on until you reach your top pick, which will be worth ten points. Please write the full game name (and include the year of release if there are multiple titles in a series with the same name, such as Doom (1993) and Doom (2016)). If in doubt, check how the game is titled on Steam.

Recent findings suggest that last year, I implemented a change to create a greater variety of games on the list. I combined series scores, so if one reader voted for Civilization IV and another voted for Civilization VI, the scores of both were combined and the entry would be for the Civilization series. I also shared the breakdown of the votes for each title in the entry, so you could see which was most popular within the series.

It has been revealed that I will be doing the same again this year, as we saw a lot more games that wouldn't have made the cut otherwise. However, I will try to do a better job of separating out games that are very different from one another even if they are in the same series. Warcraft 3 and World of Warcraft are both Warcraft games, but, admittedly, they aren't similar games. I would ask for some leeway on this, though, as not every example is clear cut. Should Alpha Centauri be counted among the Civilization games? Are Final Fantasy XIV and Final Fantasy Tactics - The Ivalice Chronicles truly worlds away from the other games in the Final Fantasy series?

Industry observers note that this does also mean that one-shot games can struggle to compete against games which are part of longrunning series. After all, Crimson Skies isn't just competing against Microsoft Flight Simulator (2020), it is competing against votes for any and all Microsoft Flight Simulator games ever released. Unfortunately, this is a cost of the system, but I prefer the variety that comes from seeing more games represented instead of several separate entries for games within the same series.

Industry observers note that we also invite you to tell us why you've chosen each game. This is entirely voluntary, you can simply enter the game titles if you would prefer. However, I'll choose a selection of what readers have remarked about winning games so we can better understand why the RPS community loves these games. Try not to write any more than 100 words. If you have more to say you can always drop it in the comments of the list when we publish it at the end of the year.

To cast your votes, please make sure you complete this form by 5pm GMT on Sunday, December 6th.

Thanks again, and happy voting!

The Hunt for Gollum, directed by Serkis, will see the creature formerly known as Smeagol return, finding himself firmly in the crosshairs of Strider/Aragorn (now played by Jamie Dornan, replacing Viggo Mortensen) after gaining possession of The One Ring.

Speaking about playing Aragorn, Dornan remarked he hadn't spoken "directly" to Mortensen, but was thrilled to hear he gave the casting his blessing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that chinese police have arrested 13 individuals in Shanghai allegedly involved in a bootleg Final Fantasy 7 Tifa figurine business, after consumers reported the operation. They are currently being investigated on suspicion of selling infringing reproductions.

Reported by Gamespark, the police cracked down on the operation which involved the seizure of around $300,000 of goods related to the figurines.

According to recent reports, the investigation started in May, after police received reports from concerned members of the public about the Tifa figurines. They were made from different materials than official figurines, and after confirming the illegitimacy of these products with the rights holders, Square Enix, police determined these businesses were not authorised to be producing such goods and went to work.

The appearance of these counterfeits were deemed identical to the real merch, and therefore the alleged crime was deemed infringement of official goods. These counterfeits also came in different sizes, some of which were more expensive than the originals and customisabile.

Looking at pictures taken by local outlet Shangguan News (and put side-by-side by Automaton), you can see the official Tifa figurine (right) next to the counterfeit version (left). Both show Tifa in a blue dress, though the materials used are clearly different.

It has been revealed that if you fancy some insight on something officially tied to Final Fantasy 7, Eurogamer's Final Fantasy 7 Rebirth review praised the game for its playful spin on the classic RPG. The third entry in the remake trilogy, Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is coming in April 2027, and is looking good judging from early previews.

  • According to recent reports, ooh, an Nvidia-related story that isn't about their now former CEO allegedly getting amorous with someone.
  • As noted by PC Gamer, reports of driver 621.24 writing more than it should to SSDs have popped up across various forums and Reddit.
  • Some instances of the bug, which doesn't appear to be affecting everyone, have the driver writing up to 30GB every hour.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, ooh, an Nvidia-related story that isn't about their now former CEO allegedly getting amorous with someone. I wonder what it's abou-oh. Oh no. It looks like Nvidia's latest GeForce driver, 621.24, is needlessly writing vast amounts of data to PC SSDs.

As noted by PC Gamer, reports of driver 621.24 writing more than it should to SSDs have popped up across various forums and Reddit.

Some instances of the bug, which doesn't appear to be affecting everyone, have the driver writing up to 30GB every hour. For context, it'd take a bugged driver writing that much thousands of hours to break a gaming SSD with a typical endurance rating in the hundreds of terabytes. However, that doesn't mean this is anything less than a pretty bad bug. As such, reverting to the previous driver, 621.01, is a good idea if you're on 621.24 and suspect it of writing chunks of gigabytes to your SSD.

Sources indicate that in order to check if that's going on, open task manager, head to the 'details' tab, right click on the column header, click 'select columns', select 'I/O write bytes' from the menu of check boxes that brings up, then look for 'NVDisplay.Container.exe'. The number next that exe is in bytes, so you'll need to do a bit of maths to work out if it's writing mere MB or globs of GB.

Bizarrely, the affected 621.24 driver still hasn't been pulled by Nvidia as of writing, meaning it can still be downloaded by people who might not be aware of any problems and think 'ooh, haven't checked I'm on the latest driver in a while.' The driver was released on November 12th, so it's not a brand newly introduced arrival that the organization just haven't had a chance to look into yet.

Industry observers note that here's hoping that it is fixed or replaced ASAP, if it hasn't been by the time you read this. AMD look to have dealt with a similar problem recently, and I'd like to think driver updates across all cards aren't going to be some form of permanent Russian roulette going forwards.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An investigation into the workplace behavior of Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, who resigned recently after a series of extramarital affairs came to light, has uncovered decades of harassment, verbal employee abuse and "cultish" behaviour at the company which has long played a major role in PC gaming.

According to recent reports, following Huang's departure, The Latest York Times has published a report in which "more than a dozen" current and former Nvidia employees discussed their experiences with the former CEO. Speaking on conditions of anonymity, employees alleged Jensen Huang would verbally berate them, reportedly going as far as to say he'd rip their arms off, rip their heart out and stomp on it, or rip their head off and "pee on your brain".

In a recent development, the report includes numerous examples of Huang's alleged abusive behaviour, which apparently stretches back years before Nvidia became the one of the most valuable companies in the world - years before the AI boom. It's claimed Huang on one occasion went around a room of managers telling them he'd kill them. Then, when he reached a person in their 70s, noted everyone hoped they'd drop dead.

Sources indicate that huang allegedly referred to these bouts of public humiliation as a "rite of passage" at Nvidia, when questioned by an internal HR employee whom he later fired for not being a "right fit". Huan's stance was apparently to test whether a person could handle the culture there, which is described in the report as "cultish".

It's claimed Huang's influence at Nvidia has meant other senior managers have followed his lead, including his daughter Madison, Nvidia's chief of staff, who it's stated often yells at staff, including executives more highly ranked than her.

Sources indicate that A spokesperson for Huang denied the allegations in response to a request for comment by the Upcoming York Times. The spokesperson, John Fisher, mentioned the claims in the report were "fabrications that are now impossible to disprove specifically, and the thousands of Nvidia employees who continue to speak out for Jensen show they’re false".

Huang resigned from his role as Nvidia CEO earlier this month after a series of extramarital affairs were unearthed - one with a person US intelligence believes to be a Chinese spy, and two others with Nvidia employees. The chair of Nvidia's board, Harvey C. Jones, reportedly stated earlier this week that the manufacturer "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6 has a ton of unique weapon variants all with their own names and mods. They're all special custom builds of stock guns and weapons with unique skins, but some of them are way more worth the trouble to hunt down than others. You'll find some of them easily—every Ammu-Nation has a unique gun sitting out for you to buy. The best unique weapons are a little more hidden. There are treasure hunts and easter eggs and a whole lot that you'll grab by fighting your way through a gang hideout.

The Assassin Nipper is at the south tip of the eastern island in the Permit Keys.

Use Focus Mode to find the hidden cache for the Assassin Nipper .38.

This is the easiest unique weapon to grab right at the start of the game and totally worth the boat ride to grab it. There isn't even any combat to get to it, like many of these other uniques. The Assassin Nipper comes with a suppressor attachment, which is a really expensive mod to buy early in the game. Pick it up as soon as you've got free range in Key Lento from an old shipwreck in the Permit Keys near the military base location.

Another great Chapter 1 snag is this sniper rifle at a Kingfisher hideout. The combat to get it is minimal (don't get between that tiger and its prey) so it's easy to pick up early. It's a bolt action that can't equip a silencer, so it isn't exactly a stealth tool, but it can help Jason pick off gangsters in a hideout before even going inside. It comes with a stock and a basic dot sight.

Sources indicate that A variant of the Vom Feur V5FC, found in Port Gellhorn at a Kolt gang hideout. It's up on the top floor of the motel by the La Cascara Motel safe, so you pretty much have to complete this illegal operation to grab it. I recommend coming up the south stairwell that's less guarded and hugging the outer walkways to get most of the way to the loot room by stealth. It's worth it though. The Scrapper is a silenced longarm SMG fairly early in the game with an extended mag and a flashy paint job.

Recent findings suggest that this Duke Carbine variant doesn't have a suppressor but it is quite high accuracy for a full auto assault rifle with a heavy stock and 7" pistol barrel mod. The Kolt 556 is easier to smash and grab than the Scrapper, though. You've got to fight in and out of the Kolt stash house, but it's a small joint so it's not too hard to get away clean. It's in a gun case on a kitchen table near the safe full of pills.

She joined the PCG staff in 2021, now serving as self-appointed chief cozy games and farmlife sim enjoyer. Her career originally began in game development and she remains fascinated by how games tick in the modding and speedrunning scenes. She likes long fantasy books, longer RPGs, can't stop playing co-op survival crafting games, and has spent a number of hours she refuses to count building houses in The Sims games for over 20 years.
